acceptanceCriteria: The check result for each component states the relation between installed and available builds, or UNKNOWN with a reason, without the caller comparing strings.
A Tasks developer-channel tag and an installed Tasks build are compared on a declared field, and a would-be downgrade is named as such.
installedVersion for tasks carries the version value, not the serialized command result; a test covers both components.
body: Observed 2026-10-01, darwin/arm64. `corvint-update check --allow-network --component tasks` returned installedVersion 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.202, installedBuild 202, availableTag tasks-dev-20260929.2, freshness RELEASE_OBSERVED, action check. `--component core` returned installedBuild 163 and availableTag v1.0.0-rc.1. Neither result carries an available build number or a comparison outcome. For Core the tag matches the installed version string, so the reader can infer it is current. For Tasks the installed version string and the dated tag share no comparable field, so an agent cannot tell from the check whether an update exists, whether the local build is newer, or whether apply would be a downgrade. Expected: the check states the relation (for example CURRENT, UPDATE_AVAILABLE, LOCAL_NEWER, or UNKNOWN with the reason). Actual: the relation is left to the caller. No update was applied in that session for this reason. Also observed: installedVersion for tasks embeds the whole JSON command result of `corvint-tasks version` as a string instead of the version value.
title: corvint-update check does not say whether the available release is newer than the installed build
